newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts to probe upside, target 110-06.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts to probe upside, target 110-06.

text.p: British gilts will make a bid for the upside on Thursday and target 110-06, provided March inflation data due later does not hold any nasty surprises, technical analysts said.
"I'm mildly bullish," said Andy Cossor, fixed income analyst at Technical Data here. "But the downside could be probed on the back of a nasty RPI figure."
Cossor said ahead of the data, the market would be confined to Wednesday's half point trading range, capped by 109-30 on the upside and 109-16 on the downside.

After the numbers are out of the way, gilts could make a break to the upside, encountering initial mild, psychological resistance at 110-00, then bumping into a more solid barrier at 110-06, said Cossor.
That level is near the 38.2 percent retracement of the major move down in gilts from the February 18 high of 113-19 to the April 1 low of 108-05.
"If we were to get above that 110-06 level, the worries would be over for gilts for a couple of weeks and we could head towards 111-00 plus," said Cossor.
The June gilt opened 9/32 higher at 109-31.
On the downside, any fall would be checked initially by congestion around 109-08,09, said Cossor, then some more around 108-29,30.
"But I can't see the market getting back down there without a move down in Bunds and or Treasuries," he added.
Chase technical analyst Guenter Redeker said the market would have to hurdle weekly trendline resistance at 110-01 to be confident of a more bullish trend.
"To improve the medium term prospects for gilts, we must have a weekly closing price above 110-01," he said.
The next target after that is 110-09, he said.
"If it moves through there, we could get further upside to 110-28 which would signal an Elliott buy signal, confirming the April 1 low of 108-05 as a bottom," said Redeker.
On the downside Redeker said congestion at 109-08 to 109-16 would hold, at least for Wednesday.

In early trade short sterling was up across the strip. By 0717 GMT, the June contract was up two basis points at 93.45, September was up three basis points at 93.20 and December was up three at 92.97.
